we introduce MIRO, an information theoretic objective for learning plannable representations that is based on maximizing the mutual information between future observations and the latent state representation.
MIRO learns representations that are robust to clutter and occlusions, and are plannable.

MIRO is a novel approach for learning representations that are both plannable and robust to the variability of the real-world, and it is a step towards developing perception systems for robotics that are applicable to the real-world while maintaining low sample complexities.
